answer: Beacon-seeded VRF admission requires each agent to commit a secret seed before a public randomness beacon fires. After the beacon, the VRF output selects one mesa from a fixed grid, and only outputs inside the current admission band may transact. Because seeds are fixed beforehand, an attacker cannot grind identities toward the band. Each attempted identity pays a fixed registration fee and a transparency-log entry; failed identities still pay, so N sybils cost N fees. The umber audit trail records every precommitment, and shale receipts bind each fee to its seed.
